confidence_semantics: publisher/source authority only; not parcel numeric accuracy

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
verified_facts: EA describes the point cloud as x/y/z source data from which site-specific DTM and DSM time-stamped raster products are derived.
Historic archiving means a matching point cloud is not guaranteed for every surface-model product.
semantic_limits: Point-cloud availability is provenance support, not the final parcel DTM sample.
A missing matching point cloud must not invalidate an otherwise documented time-stamped raster without further lineage evidence.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: EA describes the time-stamped DTM as bare-earth raster elevation produced by removing surface objects using algorithms and manual editing.
Data are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files, aligned to the OS Grid, referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn, with survey-period-specific transformation and stated +/-15cm RMSE product accuracy.
semantic_limits: The +/-15cm statement is product/survey QC context, not parcel-specific confidence.
Exact target survey date, resolution, transform and geoid still require an exact metadata match.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: EA describes the time-stamped DSM as object-inclusive elevation containing vehicles, buildings, vegetation and terrain.
The dataset is available at multiple resolutions and the metadata catalogue identifies survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
semantic_limits: DSM must not be used for bare-earth parcel extrema.
Metadata lineage may support survey provenance but does not replace a DTM sample.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model 10m
verified_facts: EA states the 10m composite DTM is resampled from the 2m composite using bilinear interpolation.
It is derived from the same time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme lineage used by other 2022 composite products.
semantic_limits: The 10m product is derived/coarse and not independent evidence against the 1m primary product.
It is unsuitable for exact parcel min/max extraction in this workflow.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied in 5km-by-5km tiles with metadata files; the national grid set contains 10,579 data tiles while the contour set has slightly fewer tiles where there are no real-world height changes.
OS states Terrain 5 is supplied by quarterly full-tile resupply.
semantic_limits: Tile resupply date is not survey capture date.
A tile reference is packaging/discovery context and not proof of target-parcel intersection.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 data structure
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 raster heights are calculated at pixel centres.
Tidal mean-high/low-water values are averaged per tile and can create a small discrete step between adjacent coastal tiles.
semantic_limits: Pixel-centre values are model samples, not guaranteed polygon extrema.
Tidal tile-edge steps require explicit coastal context before interpreting height differences.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 contour data
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 contour supply includes a per-tile metadata file with flying-date information.
Spot heights are generated automatically and z values are rounded to one decimal place.
semantic_limits: Rounded spot heights must not replace raster polygon extrema.
Contour metadata is correlated with the same OS terrain source rather than independent elevation evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Esri shapefile specification
verified_facts: OS documents separate shapefile geometry, index, attribute and projection files for contour/tideline and spot-height features.
A per-tile metadata XML file accompanies contour data.
semantic_limits: Shapefile component structure is encoding information, not a new measurement.
Equivalent OS formats remain correlated representations of one terrain product.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 GML feature types
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 contour and tideline features are represented as individual GML features and coordinates are rounded to two decimal places.
Feature attributes distinguish contour-line, spot-height and water-boundary semantics.
semantic_limits: Coordinate/attribute encoding precision is not terrain vertical accuracy.
GML feature-type distinctions do not create independent elevation observations.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 documentation root
verified_facts: OS describes Terrain 5 as a bare-earth DTM with 5m grid/contour products and quarterly publication months.
Grid and contour data derive from the same source data.
semantic_limits: Documentation-root freshness does not prove a target tile was recently surveyed.
Grid and contour agreement is correlated rather than independent validation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 product supply
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 tiled formats are supplied as 2,858 10km-by-10km tiles and may be downloaded without registration.
OS states the product is maintained by annual full-tile resupply, with publication each July.
semantic_limits: Open download availability is not target coverage proof.
Annual release date does not identify source capture date for a target parcel.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 documentation root
verified_facts: OS describes Terrain 50 as a bare-earth national DTM, with 50m grid and 10m contour forms and annual July publication.
The documentation root links current overview and technical specifications.
semantic_limits: Documentation freshness is not parcel measurement freshness.
Terrain 50 remains coarse secondary evidence only.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 GeoPackage specification
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 contours can be supplied as a national GeoPackage containing spot_height, land_water_boundary and contour_line layers.
Attribute naming differs from older formats but represents the same contour product semantics.
semantic_limits: GeoPackage is an encoding/container and does not provide an independent height observation.
Cross-format agreement cannot be counted as independent accuracy evidence.

candidates.name: Preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications (PG40s2)
verified_facts: HMLR identifies PG40 supplement 2 as guidance for preparing deed/application plans and notes an update on 13 October 2025.
semantic_limits: Application-plan guidance does not create exact parcel geometry or terrain evidence.

candidates.name: Guidance for preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications
verified_facts: HMLR states deed plans are an essential registration input and that the title plan/register cannot describe land more accurately than the pre-registration deeds allow.
semantic_limits: A compliant deed/application plan is not automatically a determined legal boundary.
Plan quality does not provide elevation measurements.

candidates.name: Other HM Land Registry plan-related services and guides (PG40s6)
verified_facts: HMLR states its computerised index map is based on Ordnance Survey mapping and indexes registered titles and pending first-registration applications.
An official SIM search can identify whether land is registered and disclose affected title numbers/types.
semantic_limits: Index-map discovery is not exact legal-boundary evidence.
Registration/title discovery is not terrain or elevation evidence.
